column3: NKJV renders the verbless “to your mouth a horn! like the eagle over the house of Yahweh” as “Set the trumpet to your mouth! He shall come like an eagle against the house of the LORD,” supplying the verbs.
Close to the Hebrew; NKJV places “Israel” as the subject at the beginning (“Israel will cry to Me”).
Close to the Hebrew; “I did not know” is rendered “I did not acknowledge them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he has rejected your calf” is rendered “Your calf is rejected,” and “my anger has burned” “My anger is aroused.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the standing grain has no growth” is rendered “The stalk has no bud.”
Close to the Hebrew; “the nations” is rendered “the Gentiles.”

NKJV renders the difficult “they have begun [to be] few from the burden of the king of princes” as “they shall sorrow a little, Because of the burden of the king of princes”; the meaning is uncertain.
Close to the Hebrew; “the numerous things of my law” is rendered “the great things of My law.”
Close to the Hebrew; “Yahweh is not pleased with them” is rendered “the LORD does not accept them.”
Close to the Hebrew; “palaces” is rendered “temples,” and “fortresses” “palaces.”
